content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Ichthyotitan severnensis: giant marine reptile | Somerset, EnglandSummarized by AI from the post belowMichio KakuArmin Motevaghe · February 19 · Shared with Public groupIchthyotitan severnensis is one of the most extraordinary marine reptiles ever discovered. It lived during the Late Triassic period, around 210 million years ago, long before the age of whales and millions of years before the rise of modern oceans. Fossils of this giant were found along the coasts of Somerset, England, especially in the Westbury Formation and Blue Anchor region. This creature belonged to the ichthyosaurs, a group of fast‑swimming marine reptiles that looked somewhat like enormous dolphins. Based on the size of its jawbones, scientists estimate that Ichthyotitan reached 20 to 25 meters in length, making it possibly the largest marine reptile ever described. Some estimates even suggest lengths over 80 feet, placing it among the greatest ocean predators of all time. Although its exact weight is unknown, a reptile of this size likely weighed many tens of tons, similar to the largest modern whales. Its huge jaws and powerful body suggest it was an apex predator, hunting much like today’s orcas; fast, intelligent, and capable of taking down large prey. Ichthyotitan lived in warm, open seas that covered what is now western Europe. These oceans were rich with fish, squid‑like creatures, and other marine reptiles, providing abundant food for such a giant.Its extinction likely came during the end‑Triassic mass extinction, a global crisis triggered by massive volcanic activity and climate change.
